correctness.rationale: C: On the specified real finite metric the transport formula is proved by matching positive and negative masses and using the hub for unmatched mass. The convex-hull generator decomposition gives all potential minimizers of the quadratic form on the unit norm ball; signed support functions and the Sherman--Morrison inverse give its exact dual maximum. Averaging any linear Euclidean pullback over the full leaf permutation group rigorously preserves its two-sided distortion inequalities, hence reduces the unrestricted problem to Q_c. Branch calculus exhaustively lists every interior stationary minimum or intersection, plus its only admissible boundary. The objective diverges at the excluded endpoints. Rational endpoint examples and a 1919-case numerical cross-check are supporting checks rather than a substitute for these universal arguments.

value.rationale: V: The metric family has a natural structural transition from a star tree (free space ℓ_1) to an equilateral configuration (type-A root polytope). Hilbert Banach--Mazur distance measures how its finite-dimensional linear geometry changes; no pointwise norm formula or isometry-group theorem answers this. The result delivers an unrestricted best-ellipsoid classification by at most O(m²) explicit algebraic candidates for all dimensions and radii, including exact nontrivial interior values. Its finite-parameter phase structure and representation-theoretic optimization are mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary table or a routine substitution.
